newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Chronology of rise of Afghan Taleban militia.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of rise of Afghan Taleban militia.

text.p: Afghan government troops appeared to be abandoning the capital Kabul on Friday with forces of the rebel Taleban Islamic militia poised on the edge of the city, witnesses said.

The Taleban movement burst onto the Afghan scene two years ago after it was formed by Islamic religious students led by Mullah Muhammad Omar. They launched a campaign against local Mujahideen guerrilla commanders who had preyed on traders at checkposts in the southern province of Kandahar.
Here is a chronology of the rise of the Islamic militia:
Oct 11: Taleban clash with local commander at Spinboldak on the Pakistan-Afghan border. Ten people are killed and 20 wounded before intermediaries stop the fighting.
Nov 4: Taleban capture provincial capital of Kandahar after rescuing a 30-truck convoy from local commanders. The convoy had been sent by Pakistan to open a trade route to Central Asia.
Taleban take Kandahar airport and a base held by a commander of Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami party, Mullah Naqib. More than 50 people are killed in four days of fighting.
Nov 29: Afghan government issues statement through its embassy in Islamabad, calling Taleban "an Islamic and humane effort".
January: Taleban capture southeastern province of Ghazni.
Feb 10: Taleban capture most of eastern province of Logar and town of Maidan Shahr, capital of Wardak province, southwest of Kabul, from Hezb-i-Islami, then in opposition.
Feb 13: Taleban capture Pul-i-Alam, capital of Logar province, from Hezb-i-Islami.
Feb 14: Taleban reach gates of Kabul, capturing Hekmatyar's Charasyab base, 25 km (15 miles) south of capital.
March 10: Taleban seize Karte Seh area of Kabul from Shi'ite Moslem Hezb-i-Wahdat group and its leader Abdul Ali Mazari.
March 11: Government forces oust Taleban from Karte Seh.
March 13: Hezb-i-Wahdat leader Abdul Ali Mazari is killed in captivity. Taleban say he died in shootout after trying to seize gun in helicopter flying him from Charasyab to Kandahar.
March 19: Troops loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani oust Taleban from Charasyab in militia's first major defeat.
Aug 3: Taleban jets force chartered Russian Ilyushin-76 cargo plane carrying ammunition for Kabul to land in Kandahar with seven Russian crew, who are held hostage.
Sept 3: Taleban capture big government air base at Shindand in western province of Farah near Iranian border.
Sept 5: Taleban capture western city of Herat from government forces which had held it since 1992. They ban girls from going to school and women from working in offices.
Oct 11: Taleban advance to gates of Kabul for second time, capturing Charasyab and later Rishkor and Khairabad hills.
Oct 14: Taleban accuse Iran of letting border be used for incursion into western Afghanistan by pro-government forces.
April 3: About 1,000 Moslem clergymen choose Taleban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar as Amir-ul-Momineen (commander of the faithful), denouncing Rabbani as unfit to lead Islamic nation.
June 1: Government confirms loss of Chaghcharan, capital of the central province of Ghor, to Taleban.
June 26: Taleban launch deadly rocket attack on Kabul, killing at least 54 people and wounding 118, as Hekmatyar resumes post of prime minister under peace deal with Rabbani.
Aug 16: Seven Russian airmen held hostage in Kandahar for over a year escape to Abu Dhabi in their own Ilyushin-76 plane.
Sept 5: Taleban launch offensive in eastern Afghanistan.
Sept 11: Taleban capture eastern city of Jalalabad and surrounding Nangarhar province adjoining Pakistan border.
Sept 13: Taleban capture eastern province of Laghman and its capital Mehtar Lam.
Sept 22: Taleban say they capture Kunar, the last eastern province held by pro-government forces.
Sept 25: Taleban say they capture strategic town of Sarobi, 70 km (31 miles) east of Kabul, and thrust north towards Bagram military airbase, 50 km (31 miles) north of the capital.
Sept 26: Afghan government troops appeared to be abandoning the capital Kabul with forces of the rebel Taleban Islamic militia poised on the edge of the city, witnesses said.
